temaNombre: The universe and the solar system
title: Space mission: the solar system
summary: Explore the universe, the planets and the solar system.
keyIdeas: The solar system contains the Sun, eight planets and their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets.
The four inner planets are rocky. The four outer planets are giants: two gas giants and two ice giants.
The Sun is our system's central star, in a spiral galaxy called the Milky Way.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica

activities.prompt: Classify these planets as rocky inner planets or giant outer planets.
activities.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants; Uranus and Neptune are ice giants with gaseous atmospheres.

activities.prompt: Aisha and Leo notice the daylight at break time. Which scientific statement correctly describes the Sun? ☀️
activities.explanation: The Sun is our solar system's star and produces its own light. Earth and other bodies orbit it.
activities.hint: Do planets produce their own light?
options: It is the largest and warmest planet in our solar system.
It is a giant moon reflecting light from distant galaxies.
It is a medium-sized star that produces light and heat through reactions inside it.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about our place in the universe.
activities.explanation: The Milky Way is the spiral galaxy containing our solar system and billions of other stars.
activities.sentence: Our solar system is inside a huge spiral galaxy called the ___.
options: Andromeda Galaxy
Milky Way
Great Bear constellation

activities.prompt: Hugo builds a scale model in Science. Order these four planets from nearest to farthest from the Sun. 🪐
activities.explanation: The full order is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

activities.prompt: On a camping trip, Omar says, 'A shooting star! A star has fallen to Earth!' What correct scientific explanation does Lucía give?
activities.explanation: A shooting star is a flash called a meteor, produced by a small particle entering the atmosphere at high speed. It is not a falling star.
activities.hint: Compare the size of a real star with Earth.
options: They are communication satellites deliberately switched off and dropped by a space agency.
They are pieces of the Sun that cool as they fall to Earth at night.
They are small particles entering the atmosphere at high speed and producing a bright flash.

activities.prompt: Match each celestial body to its description.
activities.explanation: Celestial bodies differ in size, composition and orbit.

pairs.right: An irregular rocky body orbiting the Sun; many lie between Mars and Jupiter.
An icy body that develops a bright tail of gas and dust near the Sun.
A round body orbiting the Sun that has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
A body orbiting a planet, such as our Moon.

activities.prompt: Read about space exploration and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Space telescopes help us study distant galaxies and the atmospheres of planets beyond our solar system.
activities.title: James Webb: our window on the cosmos
activities.text:
In December 2021, scientists celebrated the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope. Ground-based telescopes are affected by Earth's atmosphere and light pollution. Webb operates in space, about one and a half million kilometres from Earth.

It detects infrared light, allowing it to look through cosmic dust clouds where stars and planetary systems form. Its large, gold-coated beryllium mirrors collect faint light from early galaxies that formed more than thirteen billion years ago.

Webb also studies the atmospheres of exoplanets: planets orbiting stars other than our Sun. It looks for signs of substances such as water and carbon dioxide. The telescope shows how international scientific cooperation expands our knowledge.

questions.prompt: Why place a telescope such as Webb in space rather than on an Earth mountain?
questions.explanation: It avoids distortion by Earth's atmosphere and light pollution from towns and cities.
options: To avoid atmospheric distortion and light pollution from cities.
Stars are so close in space that no mirrors are needed.
Solar gravity does not exist in space, so no technical maintenance is needed.

questions.prompt: If Webb detects water vapour in an exoplanet's atmosphere, what can scientists reasonably conclude?
questions.explanation: Finding water is interesting, but further research is needed before making claims about life.
options: The planet once belonged to our solar system and was thrown out.
It proves with absolute certainty that complex living things inhabit the planet.
It is an interesting clue worth investigating, but does not prove that life exists there.

activities.prompt:
Martina compares orbital periods:
- Mercury: 88 Earth days
- Earth: 365 Earth days
- Jupiter: 12 Earth years

She suggests that planets farther from the Sun take longer to orbit it. A newly discovered body has an average distance beyond Neptune, whose orbit takes 165 years. What should she predict?
activities.explanation: Following the pattern, a more distant body has a larger orbit and weaker solar gravitational attraction, giving it a longer orbital period.
activities.hint: Follow the trend: Mercury < Earth < Jupiter < Neptune.
options: Exactly 365 Earth days, because all distant bodies synchronise with Earth.
More than 165 Earth years, because its orbit is larger and the Sun's gravitational pull is weaker.
Less than 88 Earth days, because outer solar system bodies travel at light speed.

activities.prompt: True or false? 'Pluto stopped being the ninth planet in 2006 because it had moved away and no longer orbited the Sun.'
activities.explanation: Pluto still orbits the Sun. It was reclassified as a dwarf planet because it has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood of other icy Kuiper Belt bodies.

activities.prompt: Adrián makes a display about the regions between planets.
activities.explanation: The main asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, separating the rocky inner planets from the giant outer planets.
activities.sentence: Between Mars and Jupiter lies the main ___ belt, containing many rocky pieces left from the solar system's formation.
options: asteroid
satellite
galaxy
